coupling: The first commit introduces a 180-byte native variants buffer, but its new IsValidVariants length check keeps every copy within that bound. The later revert commit removes that guard while retaining the native buffer path. Alone, either commit keeps the probe clean: the first still rejects overlong variants, and the second alone has no fixed-size native copy. Only their composition allows std::copy_n to write an unbounded JavaScript-provided variants string into the 180-byte stack buffer in JSLocale::ApplyOptionsToTag.
